rationale: This historical article examines Cold War labor diplomacy and the integration of Japanese trade unions (Sohyo, Zenro, ICFTU, IMF-Japan Council) into Western international labor organizations between 1949 and 1964. It has no connection to household or community water or sanitation services, legal/administrative service-access mechanisms, or water/sanitation access outcomes (E01).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both narrow and plain readings because the record is a Cold War labor-diplomacy history paper completely unrelated to water or sanitation service access (E01).

evidence_quotes.quote: Incorporating Japanese labor into the Free World: Cold War diplomacy and economic interdependence, 1949-1964
Japan's trade unions were a crucial battlefront in the Cold War. Western governments and trade unions made every effort to integrate Japanese labor into the Free World
